title: Value of a Bearer Authorization header for an Elastic token
summary: A synthetic opaque value after the Bearer scheme in an Authorization header, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map; the value has no documented prefix or width.
rationale: Elastic documents a token-service access token as a bearer token and a service account token as sent in an Authorization: Bearer header, so one header carries both families and the header does not say which. The value is flagged because of where it sits, not because of any prefix, length or alphabet, none of which the cited pages state; in particular the 22-character guaranteed secret string of a service token is not the full bearer value width and no width is assumed. The extent is the header value only: the header name, the scheme and the closing quote or brace are outside it.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value after the Bearer scheme in an Authorization header is treated as a credential whatever its shape and covered whole. Elastic documents the access token as a bearer token and the service account token as sent in an Authorization: Bearer header (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic authorization attribution are the project's decisions. No prefix, width or alphabet is claimed, and the 22-character secret component is not taken as the full value width.

sources.supports: The access token is a bearer token.
To use a service account token, include the generated token value in a request with an Authorization: Bearer header.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
